sentences.text: Christensenella minuta, the type species of the genus, is a strictly anaerobic, non-motile, non-spore-forming, Gram-negative short rod that was isolated from human faeces.
The type strain is saccharolytic, and its reported end products of glucose fermentation were acetic acid with a small amount of butyric acid.
The genus was proposed on the basis of a distinct, deep 16S rRNA lineage within the order Clostridiales, together with the new family Christensenellaceae.
A review describes Christensenella minuta as a promising next-generation probiotic because of its reported association with leanness and metabolic health.
Christensenella hongkongensis has been reported as an emerging anaerobic pathogen causing bloodstream infections, with high mortality in patients with underlying gastrointestinal malignancy.
